summary: Forest Service L-4 cab on a 10-foot tower on Teanaway Butte, built 1940; transferred to the state 1944; destroyed 1968; a tree platform is reported still there.

facts.design: 10-foot tower with a wooden L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1968; the FFLOS entry says a tree platform is still there
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (built 1940); transferred to the State in 1944

staffing.status: R.A. Spence listed as known lookout personnel in 1933; no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Willhite describes a walk up the Middle Fork route; a gate past the first bend bars motor vehicles, and the peak is a popular winter snowshoe

visit.trail_note: Park where Road 230 turns off; about two miles of road to a ridge, then a switchback hiking trail for the final few hundred feet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Willhite both give destroyed in 1968; a Willhite photo caption calls the 1968 picture a burning. Treated as one event.

sources.title: Middle Teanaway & Teanaway Butte Lookout Sites

notes_for_editor: Brief elevation 1453.6 m is not a facts key; Willhite gives summit 4,743 ft (about 1,446 m), so the brief figure may be off. Brief coordinates are within about 25 m of the firelookout.com list. The 1933 Spence entry does not say which structure he staffed, so the story keeps it apart from the 1940 build. Social posts and a Pinterest photo of the 1940 construction appeared in search but were not read or cited.
